protocol.status: frozen 2026-11-23 on Juan PC (4 vCPU / 6 GiB VM); design of the Placement campaign (C=1/16, 3 pairs, no pilot)
protocol.scope: Glance Python versus Glance Go under the same conditions: same Apache route, same MySQL server and glance database, same filesystem store and same Keystone service user (Go reads the original glance-api.conf), both with notifications noop. 12 loads x C=1/16 x 3 Python/Go pairs, same seed and random pair order; each reported value is the median of 3 pairs.

scenarios.cycle: fresh-id, create, stage (PUT /stage), import (POST /import glance-direct), import-wait (GET until active, pause import_poll_pause_s outside latency), verify-import (hashes), delete, verify-absent

scenarios.source: qemu-img convert -f raw -O qcow2 of the 16 MiB payload, made on the host
scenarios.cycle: fresh-id, create (disk_format qcow2), upload, verify-upload (hashes and virtual_size 16 MiB), delete, verify-absent
show (GET image), download (16 MiB, bytes and hashes), list (GET /v2/images?status=active&visibility=private&tag=…)

protocol.predecessor: glance-compact-v6 accepted 360/360 (Juan PC, binary a69474d, C=1/4/8/16 x 5)
protocol.acceptance: All 144 official windows valid: hashes, lengths, state, resource sampling, cleanup and original restoration verified; no minimum speedup required. No pilot (Juan): a failed window stops the campaign and it resumes from the first incomplete pair.
protocol.purpose: Measure the Glance Go binary of PR #28/#29 (Glance 100 % in Go) with the design of the Placement campaign, plus three Glance-specific loads
protocol.log_policy: Bound VM operational logs; rotate only outside measured windows, retain recent incident diagnostics and all benchmark samples
protocol.statistics: Three independent paired repetitions per cell; publish individual results, median and range; ratios are ratios of medians; no significance claim
protocol.reason: v5 limit: Go had a dedicated MySQL (128 MiB buffer pool, only its images) while Python shared DevStack MySQL (16 MiB, ~6000 tombstones). Go now uses the official catalog as in the permanent replacement. Python stays noop (stock messagingv2 exhausted descriptors in v2); Go is noop too so both do the same work.
protocol.timeout_reason: Pilot attempts 1 and 3 stopped at upload-64m C=16: a small metadata GET of the original waited 10.05 s behind 64 MiB uploads (2 uWSGI workers saturated, ~78 MiB/s for 16 clients) and hit the client 10 s timeout. 120 s, as for binary requests, records that wait as latency; requests over 10 s are counted per window (requests_over_10s). Any HTTP error, wrong bytes or failed cleanup still invalidates the window.
protocol.initial_state: Catalog purged before the campaign with the original tool: glance-manage db purge and purge_images_table, --age_in_days 0 (24157 soft-deleted images from earlier campaigns removed). Only the 2 active images remain (CirrOS, mi-cirros); Glance Go bookkeeping rows of purged images (74, phase cleaned) removed so its startup recovery has nothing orphaned.

limitations: Notification policy: Python noop, Go noop; Python without bus notifications (v3/v4); does not validate stock messagingv2 stability
Independent paired repetitions per cell; median and observed range, no statistical significance claim
Closed-loop complete cycles including drain; upload cycle includes create/verify/delete and is not pure PUT throughput
Download checks every full payload; upload load verifies active metadata/hash, worker canaries round-trip outside measured windows
Public Apache path fixed; Python caches/workers/shared DB differ from Go isolated DB/store; no language-only attribution
Python soft-delete tombstones are retained; only owned blobs and active metadata deleted via API, no SQL purge
CPU/op uses all correct contract requests in common sample interval, including verification/404; PSS at1Hz, observed peak
Per-operation percentiles preserve mixed-cycle meaning; n=3 boot or joint performance not measured here
